modelAnswer:
Eight equal sectors give probability $\frac{\text{favourable}}{8}$ per spin.
i. Rose: $\frac{1}{8}$
ii. Four-letter names (lily, rose): $\frac{2}{8}=\frac{1}{4}$
iii. Not marigold: $1-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}$
iv. Three-letter flower name: none exists here, so $\frac{0}{8}=0$.

keyPoints: List the ten faces first, then count
modelAnswer:
Outcomes on the decagonal die: $4,4,4,4,5,5,6,7,8,8$ (ten equally likely faces).
i. A four: $\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5}$
ii. Even number: $\frac{7}{10}$
iii. Multiple of four (the fours): $\frac{2}{5}$
iv. Not a seven: $\frac{9}{10}$
v. Odd number: $\frac{3}{10}$
vi. Prime number ($5,5,7$): $\frac{3}{10}$
vii. LCM of $4$ and $8$ is $8$: $\frac{2}{10}=\frac{1}{5}$
viii. HCF of $4$ and $8$ is $4$: $\frac{2}{5}$
ix. Factor of twelve ($4$ and $6$): $\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}$

keyPoints: Zero counts as a one-digit whole number here
modelAnswer:
One-digit whole numbers run from $0$ to $9$, ten values in all.
i. Less than five: $\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}$
ii. Greater than ten: $\frac{0}{10}=0$
iii. Not the largest one-digit number: $\frac{9}{10}$
iv. Additive identity of whole numbers is $0$: $\frac{1}{10}$
v. HCF of $3$ and $5$ is $1$: $\frac{1}{10}$
vi. Multiplicative identity of real numbers is $1$: $\frac{1}{10}$
vii. Not a prime number: six of ten values, $\frac{3}{5}$
viii. Factor of nine ($1,3,9$): $\frac{3}{10}$

keyPoints: Expected frequency multiplies relative frequency by trials
modelAnswer:
Relative frequencies: head $\frac{6}{10}=0.6$, tail $\frac{4}{10}=0.4$.
i. Expected heads in $520$ tosses $=0.6\times520=312$.
ii. Expected tails in $305$ tosses $=0.4\times305=122$.

keyPoints: Each expectation uses its own relative frequency
modelAnswer:

i. Six expected in $6000$ rolls: $\frac{15}{120}\times6000=750$.
ii. One expected in $3000$ rolls: $0.125\times3000=375$.

modelAnswer:
Six sections make each selection probability $\frac{1}{6}$.
a. Hazel: $\frac{1}{6}$
b. Not hazel: $1-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6}$
c. $\frac{1}{6}+\frac{5}{6}=1$, verifying unity.
d. Orchid among six selections: expected frequency $=6\times\frac{1}{6}=1$ girl.
e. Teal among sixty selections: $60\times\frac{1}{6}=10$ girls.
